title: suppress-usage-during-namespace-split-causing-underbilling
creator: Priya Nair
description: During a recent project namespace-split migration, a subset of requests were temporarily tagged with a transient namespace token that did not map to an active billing owner. This caused the metering pipeline to drop or delay attribution for those requests, resulting in undercounted usage (and underbilling) for affected projects and a mismatch between gateway logs and billing totals. The issue appears intermittently during large-scale namespace reparenting operations (split/clone flows).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create parent project P and enable delegated namespaces for split-testing.
2) Trigger automated namespace-split job to create child namespaces C1 and C2 and reassign a subset of API keys to C1.
3) Flood gateway with synthetic requests using the reparented API key during the split window.
4) Observe metering pipeline 'ingress-attribution' table: some rows show namespace_id = '<transient>' or null and never map to a project_id.
5) Compare token counts in rate-limiter logs vs billing-aggregates for the same time window to see undercount.
Notes: repro requires running the platform migration job in a staging-like topology where the namespace mapping cache is small/timed-out.
root_cause: A race between the namespace migration job and the metering attribution service. The migration writes a temporary token (ns-temp-<uuid>) to the key registry while the key mapping cache is being warm-started. Metering consumers use a fast-path that rejects unknown namespace tokens instead of falling back to historical lookup. Additionally, the rate limiter decremented its local counters when requests arrived but the metering pipeline dropped attribution rows, leading to quota underreporting for a short window.
proposed_fix: 1) Update metering attribution pipeline to accept transient namespace tokens and perform a best-effort historical lookup against the key registry when a namespace_id is unknown. 2) Change the gateway to include both canonical and pre-split namespace headers during migration windows (X-NS-Canonical and X-NS-Transient). 3) Add a short-lived reconciliation job that backfills dropped attribution rows by correlating gateway logs with raw request traces and emits corrected aggregates. 4) Introduce a feature-flag to gate the new historical-lookup code path for staged rollout.
rollback_plan: If the historical-lookup path causes regressions, flip the feature-flag off and run an emergency backfill from gateway logs (we already capture request traces for 72h). If gateway header changes break downstream consumers, revert the header inclusion in the migration orchestration and pause new namespace-splits until fixes land.
testing_plan: Unit tests for historical lookup and fallback paths; integration test that simulates namespace-split with warm cache miss; e2e in canary where we run split migrations on a single shard and validate metering totals against synthetic traffic; load test to validate reconciliation job latency under production rate (up to 20k reqs/s).
acceptance_criteria: 1) No dropped attribution rows in a simulated namespace-split on staging (verified by query totals matching gateway logs).
2) Reconciliation job backfills at least 99% of previously dropped rows in a 24h window for the test shard.
3) No observable increase in metering pipeline latency beyond SLO (+200ms p95) after enabling historical-lookup in canary.
4) Feature flag present and defaulted off for production until post-rollout verification.
